headline: High-risk default workspace overlap: ChatGPT Desktop can read local files/screens while CrewAI writes and executes tools, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run tools. That creates a plausible path where CrewAI-produced content is later treated as instructions by ChatGPT Desktop, especially via shared files or copied outputs. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into a file that ChatGPT Desktop later reads
IF the operator copies CrewAI output into ChatGPT Desktop via clipboard
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to follow instructions embedded in shared artifacts
mitigations: Use a separate workspace directory for CrewAI outputs
Disable copy-paste of CrewAI-generated artifacts into ChatGPT Desktop
Add a manual review step before ChatGPT Desktop acts on file contents
Prefix shared files with a non-executable instruction banner
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while CrewAI can read the host working directory and send data to model providers and tool integrations. If both are pointed at the same workspace or artifacts, sensitive content can flow from ChatGPT Desktop into CrewAI outputs or external APIs. The blast radius is multiple work products and sensitive local data, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents access the same project directory
IF ChatGPT Desktop reads screenshots or IDE code containing secrets
IF CrewAI forwards shared artifacts to model providers or configured tools
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use a redacted export before handing artifacts to CrewAI
Restrict CrewAI tool integrations to non-sensitive endpoints
Review ChatGPT Desktop inputs before uploading screenshots or files
requires-engineering: isolate each agent in separate containers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read local files and use vendor-mediated tools, while CrewAI can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, write files, and use broad network egress. Both can mutate the same host workspace if co-located, and CrewAI lacks default self-isolation. That overlapping write-and-execute surface makes destructive or conflicting edits likely in default setups, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory
IF CrewAI writes files that ChatGPT Desktop also reads or edits
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or per-agent isolation
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Turn on filesystem locking in the orchestrator
Run CrewAI inside a container with a private volume
Avoid letting ChatGPT Desktop edit files that CrewAI mutates
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is explicitly a multi-agent orchestration layer with shared memory and tool calls, while ChatGPT Desktop can produce file-based outputs and app-context actions. If CrewAI consumes ChatGPT Desktop output as authoritative, it can chain a mistaken or injected answer into downstream tool actions. Because CrewAI can execute tools and write files, the cascade can become irreversible quickly.
conditions: IF CrewAI treats ChatGPT Desktop output as trusted input
IF CrewAI agents act on ChatGPT Desktop-generated facts without verification
IF downstream tools can modify files, send messages, or run commands
mitigations: Require a human approval step before CrewAI tool execution
Add schema validation for ChatGPT Desktop outputs
Force CrewAI to cite source files before acting
Limit CrewAI to read-only mode for the first pass
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while CrewAI processes developer-passed data and may send it to model providers or tool integrations. If regulated data is placed into the shared workflow, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two systems. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, but the mismatch risk is real in default use.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in uploaded files or crew inputs
IF CrewAI tool integrations or model providers retain data differently than ChatGPT Desktop
IF the operator relies on one system's deletion policy for both
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Avoid regulated data in shared prompts or files
Check retention settings for both systems
Document which system stores which data class
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
